name: Kung Pao Chicken Skillet
evidence: The catalog already ships 'Slow Cooker Kung Pao Chicken Bowls' (slug slow-cooker-kung-pao-chicken-bowls): same protein (chicken) and the same named kung-pao soy/sweet sauce family — this is kung pao chicken twice, the tikka-masala-twice case, and two recipes literally named 'Kung Pao Chicken' on one site is a near-duplicate the catalog should not ship.
borderline_note: Genuine tension the decider should weigh: the candidate is the AUTHENTIC Sichuan wok version (chicken thighs, dried chilies, roasted peanuts, numbing ground Sichuan peppercorn, Chinkiang black vinegar, no rice base), whereas the catalog's kung pao is a sweet slow-cooker rice bowl (chicken breast, hoisin, honey, bell pepper, zucchini) with NO peanuts, dried chili, or Sichuan pepper — arguably a misnomer. Method (wok stir-fry vs slow cooker) and starch (dish-only vs rice bowl) differ, so on the strict 4-factor test only 2 of 4 match. If the catalog wants an authentic Sichuan replacement, this candidate is the stronger, more legitimate kung pao. But by dish-name/concept identity it is a duplicate; ruling DUPE to protect against shipping two 'Kung Pao Chicken' plates.
cross_protein_collisions: Any kung pao in another selector's pool built on a different protein (kung pao beef, kung pao pork, kung pao shrimp/tofu) is STRUCTURALLY the same dish — same dried-chili + peanut + Sichuan-peppercorn soy/vinegar sauce, only the protein swapped. Decider should catch a kung-pao-<other-protein> twin. Note: catalog's sichuan-dan-dan-noodles-with-pork is a DIFFERENT dish (dan dan noodles), not a collision.
